Algebra I · Lesson 5.3

Elimination

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Lesson 5.2 closed on a system with no clean isolate, 9x+7y=769x+7y=76 and 5x+8y=725x+8y=72. Every coefficient is bigger than 11, so solving for a letter starts with a division, y=76−9x7y=776−9x​, and fractions appear in every line after that. Set the system aside. It returns as the last problem of this lesson.

Problem
At the solution of the system 4x+7y=504x+7y=50 and 3x−7y=133x−7y=13, each equation's two sides are the same number, so the sum of the left sides equals the sum of the right sides. Write that sum equation, combine like terms on each side, then solve what remains and enter xx.
Show a hint
  • Stack the two equations and add straight down, left side to left side and right side to right side.
  • The +7y+7y and −7y−7y sum to zero, so the sum equation is 7x=637x=63.
Show the full solution
Adding the two left sides and the two right sides gives 7x+0y=637x+0y=63, so 7x=637x=63 and x=9x=9​. Back-substituting, 7y=50−36=147y=50−36=14, so y=2y=2, and (9,2)(9,2) checks in both originals, 36+14=5036+14=50 and 27−14=1327−14=13. One addition removed yy and left a chapter 4 equation.
Key idea
Elimination. When the same letter carries opposite coefficients in the two equations, adding the equations term by term makes that letter's terms sum to zero, and one letter remains. Chapter 4 solves the equation that is left, and substituting the value back into either original gives the partner. The addition is legal because at a solution pair both equations are true, so adding the left sides and the right sides adds equal numbers to equal numbers. Every solution of the system satisfies the sum equation too, so no solution is lost.
Problem
Solve the system 7x+3y=97x+3y=9 and 2x−3y=182x−3y=18 by adding the equations, then back-substitute into either original. The ask is yy, not xx.
Show a hint
  • The opposite yy-coefficients cancel when the equations are added, but the sum equation has no yy in it, so it cannot answer the ask by itself.
  • Adding gives 9x=279x=27. Find xx, then substitute that value into either original equation.
Show the full solution
Adding gives 9x=279x=27, so x=3x=3. Then 21+3y=921+3y=9, 3y=−123y=−12, and y=−4y=−4​. Elimination finds one letter and back-substitution finds the other, so stopping at x=3x=3 leaves the ask unanswered.
Problem
The yy-coefficients of 7x+2y=627x+2y=62 and 3x+2y=303x+2y=30 are equal, not opposite, so adding gives 10x+4y=9210x+4y=92 and both letters are still there. Subtract the second equation from the first instead, every term on both sides, back-substitute, and enter x+yx+y.
Show a hint
  • Subtracting equal numbers from equal numbers is as legal as adding them, and equal coefficients cancel under subtraction.
  • The left sides subtract term by term, 7x−3x7x−3x and 2y−2y2y−2y, and the right sides subtract as well.
Show the full solution
Subtracting gives 4x+0y=324x+0y=32, so x=8x=8. Then 56+2y=6256+2y=62, 2y=62y=6, y=3y=3, and x+y=11x+y=11​. The subtraction has to reach the right sides too, 62−30=3262−30=32, not only the columns of letters.
Key idea
Subtract the whole equation. Subtracting equal numbers from equal numbers also leaves equal results, so one equation can be subtracted from the other, and matching coefficients cancel that way. The minus stands in front of the entire equation being subtracted, so it reaches every one of its terms, signs included, the same rule 4.4 applied to a minus in front of parentheses. The right sides subtract too. The common error is flipping the sign in the matched column and copying the rest, which writes a different equation and lands on a pair that fails the check.
Problem
Subtracting 5x−2y=345x−2y=34 from 5x+3y=745x+3y=74, a student writes 3y−2y=403y−2y=40, so y=40y=40, and the check fails. Find the sign the student dropped, redo the subtraction with every term carrying its sign, and enter the correct yy.
Show a hint
  • Subtracting a whole equation subtracts each of its terms, signs included. Look at what the second equation's yy-term actually is.
  • That term is −2y−2y, so the yy-column is 3y−(−2y)3y−(−2y), not 3y−2y3y−2y. Redo it, then the right sides.
Show the full solution
The yy-column is 3y−(−2y)=5y3y−(−2y)=5y and the right sides give 74−34=4074−34=40, so 5y=405y=40 and y=8y=8​. Subtracting a whole equation puts a minus in front of parentheses, the rule from 4.4, since the left column means 5x+3y−(5x−2y)5x+3y−(5x−2y). The student subtracted 2y2y instead of −2y−2y.

Matched coefficients are luck. When neither equation offers one, 4.2 allows multiplying an equation, both sides, by any nonzero number, and the result is an equivalent equation with the same solutions. So a matching coefficient can be built. Multiply one equation by whatever number its coefficient needs, then add or subtract.

Problem
In 3x+4y=593x+4y=59 and 6x+5y=856x+5y=85, no coefficient matches yet. Multiply the first equation, both sides, by 22, then subtract to eliminate xx. Solve the system and enter x+yx+y.
Show a hint
  • Write the doubled first equation out in full, then subtract the second from it column by column, the xx terms, the yy terms, and the right sides.
  • The doubled first equation is 6x+8y=1186x+8y=118. Subtract the second equation from that one.
Show the full solution
Doubling the first equation gives 6x+8y=1186x+8y=118, and subtracting the second leaves 3y=333y=33, so y=11y=11. Then 3x+44=593x+44=59 gives x=5x=5, and x+y=16x+y=16​. The scaling has to reach the right side, so the doubled equation ends in 118118, not 5959.
Problem
Solve 7x+5y=−17x+5y=−1 and 3x+15y=−393x+15y=−39. Scale the first equation by 33, subtract the second, and enter yy. Both right sides are negative, so the subtraction there needs care.
Show a hint
  • Tripling the first equation makes both yy-columns 15y15y. Scale both sides, so the −1−1 is tripled as well.
  • The right sides subtract as −3−(−39)−3−(−39), a difference of two negatives.
Show the full solution
Tripling the first equation gives 21x+15y=−321x+15y=−3, and subtracting the second leaves 18x=−3−(−39)=3618x=−3−(−39)=36, so x=2x=2. Then 14+5y=−114+5y=−1 gives 5y=−155y=−15 and y=−3y=−3​. The tripled right side is −3−3, not −1−1, and subtracting −39−39 adds 3939.
Key idea
Scale both, and pick the cheap letter. When neither coefficient of the chosen letter divides the other, multiply each equation by the number its coefficient needs to reach a common multiple of the two, then add or subtract. Either letter can be eliminated and both choices give the same pair, so the choice is only about the size of the arithmetic. The habit is to eliminate the letter whose two coefficients have the smaller common multiple, which keeps every number in the run small.
Problem
In 6x+7y=566x+7y=56 and 3x+5y=313x+5y=31, one letter eliminates by scaling a single equation, while the other needs both equations scaled to reach 3535. Pick the cheap one, solve the system, and enter the product xyxy.
Show a hint
  • Price the two choices before scaling anything. The xx-coefficients are 66 and 33, the yy-coefficients are 77 and 55.
  • Doubling the second equation makes both xx-columns 6x6x. Subtract, and a yy-equation is left.
Show the full solution
Doubling the second equation gives 6x+10y=626x+10y=62, and subtracting the first leaves 3y=63y=6, so y=2y=2. Then 6x+14=566x+14=56 gives x=7x=7, and xy=14xy=14​. Eliminating yy reaches the same pair, but it means scaling to 35y35y and subtracting 280−217280−217 instead of 62−5662−56.
Problem
Eliminate yy from 5x+4y=465x+4y=46 and 7x−6y=−407x−6y=−40 by scaling both equations so the yy-terms become 12y12y and −12y−12y. Solve the system, check the pair in both originals, and enter the product xyxy.
Show a hint
  • Each equation gets multiplied by whatever its yy-coefficient needs to reach 1212, and the factor hits both sides, right side included.
  • The scaled yy-terms are 12y12y and −12y−12y, which are opposites, so the two equations are added rather than subtracted.
Show the full solution
Three times the first is 15x+12y=13815x+12y=138, twice the second is 14x−12y=−8014x−12y=−80, and adding them gives 29x=5829x=58, so x=2x=2. Then 10+4y=4610+4y=46 gives y=9y=9, and xy=18xy=18​. Check (2,9)(2,9) in both originals, 10+36=4610+36=46 and 14−54=−4014−54=−40.
Fun fact
The Chinese Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art, compiled roughly two thousand years ago, solves systems of linear equations in its fangcheng chapter by elimination on an array of counting rods, long before the method had a European name.
Problem
Solve 4x+9y=324x+9y=32 and 2x+7y=212x+7y=21 by eliminating xx. Every line stays whole until one final division. Enter xx as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Doubling the second equation matches the xx-columns at 4x4x.
  • yy comes out whole. Put that yy back into either equation and the coefficient of xx will not divide the right side evenly, which is where the fraction finally shows up.
Show the full solution
Doubling the second equation gives 4x+14y=424x+14y=42, and subtracting the first leaves 5y=105y=10, so y=2y=2. Then 2x+14=212x+14=21 gives 2x=72x=7 and x=72x=27​​. Every line before that division stayed whole, so the only fraction in the problem is the answer itself.

Both letters can cancel at once. When they do, what remains is a statement about numbers alone, true or false on its own. Substitution reached the same situation in 5.2, and the reading is the same here. The leftover statement is a verdict on the whole system, and the next two problems have one of each kind.

Problem
Try elimination on 2x+6y=352x+6y=35 and 3x+9y=483x+9y=48. Scale the first equation by 33 and the second by 22, then subtract. Both letters cancel and a statement about numbers is left. Decide what it means and enter the number of solutions of the system.
Show a hint
  • When both letter columns cancel, the number statement left behind is the verdict on the whole system.
  • Both scalings give the left side 6x+18y6x+18y, while the right sides come out 105105 and 9696. Subtract and read what is left.
Show the full solution
The scaled equations are 6x+18y=1056x+18y=105 and 6x+18y=966x+18y=96, and subtracting gives 0=90=9, false at every pair, so the system has 00​ solutions. That is 5.1's count for conflicting claims, reached here by elimination and in 5.2 by substitution.
Key idea
When both letters vanish. A false statement like 0=90=9 means the two claims conflict at every pair, so the system has no solution, 5.1's count of zero. A true statement like 0=00=0 means one equation is a scaled copy of the other, so the two make the same claim, every pair solving one solves both, and the solutions are infinitely many. Elimination is not failing in either case. It is reporting the count.
Problem
Eliminating on 3x−5y=123x−5y=12 and 6x−10y=246x−10y=24 leaves 0=00=0, true at every pair, so the system has infinitely many solutions. That does not make every pair a solution. Of (4,0)(4,0), (19,9)(19,9), (14,6)(14,6), (8,2)(8,2), enter how many solve the system.
Show a hint
  • 0=00=0 means the second equation is a scaled copy of the first, so a pair solves the system exactly when it solves 3x−5y=123x−5y=12.
  • Substitute each listed pair into 3x−5y=123x−5y=12 and count the ones that give 1212.
Show the full solution
In 3x−5y3x−5y the four pairs give 1212, 1212, 1212, and 24−10=1424−10=14, so 33​ of them solve the system. Infinitely many solutions means every pair satisfying the shared equation, not every pair anybody writes down.

Back to the shelved system. In 9x+7y=769x+7y=76 and 5x+8y=725x+8y=72 no letter isolates without a division, which is what stopped substitution. Elimination isolates nothing, so no division is needed. The xx-coefficients 99 and 55 both divide 4545, so scaling the first equation by 55 and the second by 99 puts 45x45x in each.

Problem
Finish the system 5.2 left unsolved. Scale 9x+7y=769x+7y=76 by 55 and 5x+8y=725x+8y=72 by 99, so both carry 45x45x, then subtract and solve. Enter yy as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Multiplying an equation through by a number keeps the same solution pair, so scaling is safe. The target 4545 is the smallest number that both 99 and 55 divide into.
  • Five times the first equation is 45x+35y=38045x+35y=380 and nine times the second is 45x+72y=64845x+72y=648. One subtraction and one division are left.
Show the full solution
The scaled equations are 45x+35y=38045x+35y=380 and 45x+72y=64845x+72y=648, and subtracting the first from the second leaves 37y=26837y=268, so y=26837y=37268​​, with x=10437x=37104​. The work stays in whole numbers until that last division, while isolating a letter in either original equation would start with a division.

Both methods solve every linear system in two variables, so the choice is convenience. An equation already solved for a letter, or a letter with coefficient 11 or −1−1, points to substitution. Coefficients that match, or match after one scaling, point to elimination. Lesson 5.4 takes on systems that need cleanup before either method applies.

Practice these ideas

Practice
The yy-terms of 6x+5y=576x+5y=57 and 3x−5y=63x−5y=6 are +5y+5y and −5y−5y. Add the left sides and add the right sides, solve the one-letter equation that remains, and enter xx.
Show the solution
Adding gives 9x=639x=63, so x=7x=7​, and 5y=57−42=155y=57−42=15 gives y=3y=3. Check in the second equation, 21−15=621−15=6.
Practice
Solve 6x+y=406x+y=40 and 3x−y=143x−y=14 by adding the two equations, then back-substituting into either original. Enter yy.
Show the solution
Adding gives 9x=549x=54, so x=6x=6, and 6(6)+y=406(6)+y=40 gives y=4y=4​. Check in the second equation, 3(6)−4=143(6)−4=14. Adding removes one letter and back-substitution finds the other.
Practice
The xx-terms of −4x+9y=42−4x+9y=42 and 4x+11y=784x+11y=78 are already opposites, so adding removes xx and leaves an equation in yy. Solve the system and enter xx.
Show the solution
Adding the equations gives 20y=12020y=120, so y=6y=6. The first equation becomes −4x+54=42−4x+54=42, so −4x=−12−4x=−12 and x=3x=3​. The second equation checks, 4(3)+11(6)=12+66=784(3)+11(6)=12+66=78.
Practice
Two numbers add to 9494 and differ by 2222. Write the two facts as a system, add the equations to eliminate a letter, and enter the smaller number.
Show the solution
The system is x+y=94x+y=94 and x−y=22x−y=22. Adding gives 2x=1162x=116, so x=58x=58, and 58+y=9458+y=94 gives y=36y=36​. Check, 58−36=2258−36=22. A sum fact and a difference fact always add straight to a one-letter equation.
Practice
The yy-coefficients of 9x+5y=1209x+5y=120 and 4x+5y=704x+5y=70 are both 55, equal rather than opposite, so adding keeps both letters. Subtract the second equation from the first instead, every term on both sides, and enter xx.
Show the solution
Subtracting the second equation from the first gives 5x=505x=50, so x=10x=10​. Then 5y=70−40=305y=70−40=30 gives y=6y=6, and the first equation checks, 90+30=12090+30=120. Subtracting the other way gives −5x=−50−5x=−50 and the same xx.
Practice
Subtract 2x−3y=−112x−3y=−11 from 2x+6y=522x+6y=52. The xx-column cancels. Finish the solve and enter xx.
Show the solution
Subtracting gives 9y=639y=63, so y=7y=7, and 2x+42=522x+42=52 gives 2x=102x=10 and x=5x=5​. The pair checks in 2x−3y=−112x−3y=−11, since 10−21=−1110−21=−11. Both the −3y−3y and the −11−11 flipped sign when that equation was subtracted.
Practice
Both 7x+5y=817x+5y=81 and 7x−3y=−157x−3y=−15 lead with 7x7x. Subtract the second equation from the first, flipping the sign of every term of the subtracted equation, the right side included. Enter yy.
Show the solution
Subtracting term by term, 5y−(−3y)=8y5y−(−3y)=8y and 81−(−15)=9681−(−15)=96, so 8y=968y=96 and y=12y=12​. Back-substituting gives x=3x=3, and 7(3)−3(12)=21−36=−157(3)−3(12)=21−36=−15 checks the second equation. Writing 5y−3y5y−3y instead of 5y+3y5y+3y is the usual slip.
Practice
In 8x+5y=738x+5y=73 and 4x+15y=994x+15y=99, scaling the first equation once makes the yy-coefficients match. Make that match, eliminate yy, and enter xx.
Show the solution
Three times the first equation is 24x+15y=21924x+15y=219, and subtracting the second gives 20x=12020x=120, so x=6x=6​. Then 48+5y=7348+5y=73 gives y=5y=5, and 4(6)+15(5)=994(6)+15(5)=99 checks. Scaling has to reach the right side too.
Practice
Solve 5x+9y=875x+9y=87 and 10x+7y=8610x+7y=86. Doubling the first equation, both sides, lines up the xx-terms at 10x10x. Enter yy.
Show the solution
Twice the first equation is 10x+18y=17410x+18y=174. Subtracting the second gives 11y=8811y=88, so y=8y=8​, with x=3x=3 from 5x+72=875x+72=87. Check in the second equation, 30+56=8630+56=86.
Practice
No coefficients in 9x+y=439x+y=43 and 5x+3y=195x+3y=19 match yet, but one scaling of the first equation, both sides, brings the yy-columns together. Solve the system and enter yy.
Show the solution
Three times the first equation is 27x+3y=12927x+3y=129. Subtracting the second gives 22x=11022x=110, so x=5x=5, and 45+y=4345+y=43 gives y=−2y=−2​. Check in the second equation, 25−6=1925−6=19.
Practice
For 3x+7y=413x+7y=41 and 12x+9y=6912x+9y=69, the xx-coefficients first meet at 1212 and the yy-coefficients first meet at 6363. Enter the letter that is cheaper to eliminate.
Show the solution
Matching at 12x12x takes one scaling, the first equation times 44, while matching at 63y63y takes two, the first times 99 and the second times 77, so the cheaper letter is xx​. Both routes end at the same pair (2,5)(2,5), and the only difference is how large the numbers get.
Practice
Solve 6x+7y=756x+7y=75 and 4x+5y=514x+5y=51. Neither xx-coefficient divides the other, so scale both equations to eliminate xx. Enter the product xyxy.
Show the solution
Twice the first is 12x+14y=15012x+14y=150 and three times the second is 12x+15y=15312x+15y=153. Subtracting gives y=3y=3, and 6x+21=756x+21=75 gives 6x=546x=54 and x=9x=9, so xy=27xy=27​. Check in the second equation, 36+15=5136+15=51.
Practice
The xx-coefficients of 2x+3y=162x+3y=16 and 7x+5y=237x+5y=23 are 22 and 77, whose only common factor is 11. Scale both equations to a common xx-coefficient, subtract, and enter xx.
Show the solution
Seven times the first is 14x+21y=11214x+21y=112 and twice the second is 14x+10y=4614x+10y=46. Subtracting gives 11y=6611y=66, so y=6y=6, and 2x+18=162x+18=16 gives 2x=−22x=−2 and x=−1x=−1​. Check in the second equation, −7+30=23−7+30=23. A solution pair can have a negative member.
Practice
Solve 7x+9y=297x+9y=29 and 6x+3y=176x+3y=17. Nothing here is fractional until the last step. Enter yy as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Three times the second equation is 18x+9y=5118x+9y=51, and subtracting the first gives 11x=2211x=22, so x=2x=2. Then 6(2)+3y=176(2)+3y=17 gives 3y=53y=5 and y=53y=35​​. Check in the first equation, 7(2)+9⋅53=14+15=297(2)+9⋅35​=14+15=29.
Practice
Eliminate a letter from 3x+8y=443x+8y=44 and 6x+16y=776x+16y=77. Both letters cancel at once and a number statement is left. Read it and enter the number of solutions of the system.
Show the solution
Twice the first equation is 6x+16y=886x+16y=88. Subtracting the second gives 0=110=11, false at every pair, so the system has 00​ solutions. The same left side cannot be 8888 and 7777 at once, so the two equations contradict each other and no pair passes both.
Practice
Elimination on 5x−2y=155x−2y=15 and 15x−6y=4515x−6y=45 leaves 0=00=0, true everywhere, so the system has infinitely many solutions. That does not make every pair one of them. Of (3,0)(3,0), (5,5)(5,5), (6,7)(6,7), (4,1)(4,1), enter how many solve the system.
Show the solution
The left sides are 15−0=1515−0=15, 25−10=1525−10=15, 30−14=1630−14=16, and 20−2=1820−2=18, so 22​ of the four solve the system. Infinitely many solutions means every pair satisfying the shared equation, and only those.
Practice
For exactly one value of kk, elimination on 8x+12y=3728x+12y=372 and 2x+3y=k2x+3y=k leaves 0=00=0 and the system has infinitely many solutions. Every other value of kk leaves a false statement instead. Enter kk.
Show the solution
Since 8x+12y8x+12y is 44 times 2x+3y2x+3y, the two claims agree at every pair exactly when 372=4k372=4k, so k=93k=93​. Check, multiplying 2x+3y=932x+3y=93 by 44 gives 8x+12y=3728x+12y=372. Any other value makes one left side equal two different numbers, and the count drops to zero.
Practice
Solve 10x+6y=16210x+6y=162 and 7x+9y=1477x+9y=147. One letter's coefficients meet at 1818 and the other's meet at 7070. Eliminate the cheaper one, scaling both equations, and enter the product xyxy.
Show the solution
Three times the first is 30x+18y=48630x+18y=486 and twice the second is 14x+18y=29414x+18y=294. Subtracting gives 16x=19216x=192, so x=12x=12, and 120+6y=162120+6y=162 gives 6y=426y=42 and y=7y=7, so xy=84xy=84​. Check in the second equation, 84+63=14784+63=147. Eliminating xx instead would push the scaled equations past 10001000.
